envImpact.why: sync-registry-credentials clones and syncs a Secret; on 1.13 the background controller loses both the wildcard read (the view role excludes Secrets) and the chart's default Secret write grant, the values set no rbac extraResources, and no ClusterRole aggregates secrets to the background controller — regcred stops being created in new namespaces.

The values pin features.policyExceptions.enabled=true (so the default flip alone looks harmless) but leave the namespace empty; v1.13.0 then logs "the flag --exceptionNamespace cannot be empty" and installs no exception selector, so both v2beta1 PolicyExceptions stop applying and the exempted ebpf-exporter DaemonSet and ingress-nginx-controller Deployment are denied by the Enforce policies.
require-team-label and disallow-privileged-containers set spec.validationFailureAction (and require-team-label the overrides); they keep working on 1.13 but use the deprecated policy-level fields.

The cluster has generate policies (the deprecated switch's natural home) but none sets spec.generateExisting, spec.generateExistingOnPolicyUpdate or spec.mutateExistingOnPolicyUpdate, and there are no mutate-existing policies; the manifests are the complete policy set.

Every chart image is pulled from registry.corp.example (global.image.registry) and the mirror list only carries bitnami/kubectl:1.28.5; policyReportsCleanup is left at its default (enabled), so the v1.13.0 post-upgrade hook pulls registry.corp.example/bitnami/kubectl:1.30.2, which does not exist, and the Helm upgrade fails on the hook.
both PolicyExceptions are applied as kyverno.io/v2beta1, deprecated in 1.13 (still served); the GitOps manifests should move to kyverno.io/v2.

Kyverno is upgraded with Helm, crds.migration.enabled and templating.enabled are left at their defaults (true / false), so the post-upgrade migrate-resources hook rewrites the stored objects; the manual kube-storage-version-migrator step does not apply.

metricsConfig.metricsExposure is not set, so the new chart default disables resource_namespace on kyverno_policy_results_total, and the KyvernoPolicyFailuresByNamespace alert groups by exactly that label — it collapses into a single series without the namespace.

the values tune cleanupJobs.ephemeralReports / clusterEphemeralReports / updateRequests; the v1.13.0 chart no longer has those keys or CronJobs, so the tuning is silently dropped and the circuit breakers govern instead.
Kubernetes 1.29 is inside both the 1.12.x (1.26–1.29) and the 1.13.x (1.28–1.31) tested ranges; confirm, do not flag.
